correctedState:
Confirmed, with corrected cites and a wider scope than filed.

CITES: `packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/goal-service.ts:248-259` (not :246-259), `:151-155` (not :149-153), `:480` (not :476). Add the enforcing invariant `:555` (`validTerminalState` demands `source === 'manual'` + non-empty evidence for `complete`) and the loop that proves the consequence, `packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:3376-3398`.

SCOPE — the filed claim understates the gap in one direction and overstates it in another.

Understates: Nessy has no `/goal` command or any user surface at all. `grep -ran goal_create apps/ packages/` finds the action only in the protocol type (`core/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:346`), its parser (`shared/protocol/pi-harness-runtime.ts:295`) and the SessionManager arm (`:3279`) — no renderer ever sends it. In the shipped app the only producer is the model, through the pi-only `Goal` tool (`session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:991`), whose port hardcodes `source: 'agent', creator: 'pi'` (`SessionManager.ts:12148-12156`). So the page's premise — the USER types a condition and a fresh model decides completion — is absent; what exists is a model-owned, self-managed goal whose evaluator is deliberately advisory (`:480` 'Advisory goal check only. You have no tools and cannot change goal state.').

Overstates: the extra spend is bounded, unlike Claude's. `DEFAULT_PI_GOAL_BUDGETS` (`:14-19`) caps a goal at 32 turns / 250k tokens / $20 / 2h and `enforceBudgetsLocked` (:284) terminates it as `budget_exhausted`; Claude's `/goal` has no such cap (the page tells you to write a turn clause into the condition text). And a `complete_suggested` normally costs one extra turn, not an unbounded run, because the continuation prompt surfaces the verdict and instructs `Goal complete`.

CONTEXT, not an exemption: the parity audit already triaged this feature away from a row — `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-nessy-claude-parity-audit.md:1722` lists "`/goal` as a *completion condition*" under 'Minor, no row, listed for completeness'. That is a scoping judgement about priority, not a recorded decision that the advisory verdict is correct, so the divergence remains open and unowned.
